newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU revises air liability rules, trims figure.
newsitem.headline: EU revises air liability rules, trims figure.

text.p: European Union transport ministers tied up rules for a fast-track system on Thursday obliging airlines to pay compensation to air travellers or their relatives after an air crash, an EU official said.

But ministers trimmed a minimum, non-refundable payout airlines will have to make to victims or their dependents in the immediate aftermath of a crash, cutting it from the 50,000 Ecus ($63,000) proposed by the European Commission to 15,000 Ecus, officials said after the meeting.
The proposals will make airlines strictly liable for 100,000 Ecus per person in the event of a crash, meaning they could not exclude or limit their liability for that sum by proving no fault.
Ministers also agreed that new liability rules would apply to all EU carriers but not to those of third countries operating to and from airports in the 15-country bloc.
A Commission spokesman told reporters that final adoption of the rules, which would signal their immediate entry into force, now depended on Euro-MPs' agreement.

The proposal would protect passengers from terrorist attacks where there is currently no cover. Carriers would be required to pay out the 15,000 Ecus compensation within 10 days of a passenger's death or up to a ceiling of 15,000 Ecus in the event of injury, it said.

Ministers ruled out the Commission's proposal that crash victims or their dependents be able to pursue court action in their home courts rather than in the carrier's country of origin, its main place of business or at the beginning or end of the ticketed journey.
The proposal will abolish the current $10,000 ceiling on passenger liability in the event of injury or death in a crash and extend the liability cover to domestic flights in the 15-country bloc.
Existing rules, as defined under 1929 Warsaw Convention and other agreements, currently apply only to international flights.
